idea-plugin.name: PrismTabs
idea-plugin.description:
Colour-coded tab groups for IntelliJ editor tabs.

Right-click a tab for the colour swatch popup: pick one of 8 preset colours to start a new group and name it, or "Add to Group…" to put the tab in a group you already have. "Manage Groups…" lets you list a group's files, rename, recolour, delete, or mark a group active — files opened while a group is active join it automatically, and a file that was already open joins it in one click, from the same popup.

The PrismTabs tool window lists every group with its colour and member count, expands each one to the files it holds, and can hide a group (closing its tabs, remembering them) or show it again. Right-clicking one of those files removes it from its group — no need to open the file first, which is the one thing a tab's own menu cannot offer. Assignments persist across restarts, along with the tabs a hidden group remembers, and follow a file through a rename or move. The preset palette itself is editable under Settings | Tools | PrismTabs.

Free forever
  • Assign tabs to 8 preset colours, each measured for contrast on both light and dark editor tabs
  • Unlimited named groups — create, rename, recolour, delete
  • "Files…" lists everything in a group, open tab or not, and reopens any of it
  • Assignments persist across restarts and survive file renames and moves
Paid — a 30-day free trial on every new install, then a subscription
  • The PrismTabs tool window for managing every group at a glance, each group expanding to the files it holds
  • Hide a group to close its tabs and remember them, then show it to reopen them together
  • Mark a group active so newly opened files join it automatically
  • Rename or repaint any preset colour under Settings | Tools | PrismTabs
When the trial ends, PrismTabs drops to the Free tier — never a lockout. Your groups and colours stay either way.

prismtabs.com has the manual, the tier breakdown and the licence agreement. Bugs and feature requests, for every edition, go to the public feedback tracker — anything touching a purchase should be emailed instead, as that tracker is public.
